allowed_changes: register additive product-owned workspace crates
add workspace dependencies used by product-owned crates
refresh Cargo.lock through the pinned toolchain
forbidden_changes: changing upstream feature defaults to force provider behavior
replacing upstream dependency versions unrelated to the product crates
hand-editing Cargo.lock

allowed_changes: register provider-neutral capability ports and typed outcomes
mount product-owned application routers or retained operations
carry exact scope, deadline, cancellation, provenance, and terminal state
forbidden_changes: provider-name branching
concrete NCM or OCEAN types in public TraceDecay contracts
silent fallback or fake readiness

allowed_changes: define a provider-neutral advisory cognitive-recall port
carry exact scope, deadline, cancellation, provenance, and typed degradation
add focused application and production-reachability contract tests
forbidden_changes: provider-name branching or concrete provider types
provider authority over canonical facts or final context assembly
silent fallback or fabricated empty success

allowed_changes: construct and retain product-owned capability registries and lifecycle ports
inject provider-neutral observation, recall, feedback, maintenance, and inspection capabilities
bind exact project/worktree/provider scope at startup
retain the composed dormant host across the daemon and MCP project-server lifetime
forbidden_changes: provider implementation logic in the composition root
global mutable provider singleton
unbounded worker or queue
provider authority over source, sessions, Native facts, or configuration

allowed_changes: propagate one caller-supplied absolute deadline through daemon shutdown layers
bound blocking drain work by the caller deadline's remaining budget
report Failed for incomplete shutdown while completing terminal teardown
forbidden_changes: creating a fresh deadline budget in a nested shutdown layer
hiding incomplete shutdown behind a successful terminal
reordering unrelated daemon lifecycle phases
adding provider or memory integration logic

allowed_changes: use the deadline-aware shutdown API in the production test-transport harness
reuse one absolute deadline across invocation and detached-server teardown
forbidden_changes: creating a fresh deadline budget between production-harness teardown stages
reordering unrelated production-harness teardown phases
adding provider or memory integration logic

allowed_changes: select an explicit or Cargo-provided same-checkout CLI and otherwise fail closed
clear inherited daemon routing and use one bounded production-equivalent socket path
share the common isolated command environment across the memory integration suite
remove a platform gate from a test-only import so an upstream lib-test module compiles on every supported host
forbidden_changes: guessing a sibling profile binary
reusing an installed daemon or global profile
silently mixing checkout revisions
changing production behavior
changing any upstream test body, assertion, or fixture while fixing its compilation

allowed_changes: fan out an already-admitted normalized observation into a bounded product-owned dispatcher
attach stable operation identity and exact scope after canonical ingest or settlement
forbidden_changes: blocking or changing canonical host ingest in observer mode
host-specific provider logic
provider output affecting prompts or external actions

allowed_changes: invoke provider-neutral bounded advisory recall
carry an advisory, provenance-labelled provider-memory lane into MCP context assembly
validate provenance, freshness, exact scope, policy, deadline, and cancellation before context assembly
report typed per-lane coverage and degradation
forbidden_changes: provider constructing the final context envelope
provider candidate replacing current code truth
cross-worktree or cross-session candidate reuse
silent fallback to another provider

allowed_changes: emit idempotent provider feedback/outcome observations after canonical settlement
record typed dispatch receipts without changing the settled result
forbidden_changes: provider directly changing Native trust
post-commit provider failure becoming canonical operation failure
provider-specific transport schema

allowed_changes: register provider-neutral configuration keys and capability selection
pin explicit observer/active mode and provider instance scope
forbidden_changes: provider self-activation
provider names outside registry/adapter construction
credentials embedded in public configuration values
configuration bypassing transactional revision and audit

allowed_changes: call the existing host-neutral transcript ingest route from a host lifecycle event under an explicit, bounded time budget
register an additional project-scoped transcript-capture kernel for a host that already has a profile-scoped kernel, reusing the session-sync ingest pass
declare an opt-in, default-off product test target and the feature it requires in the tracedecay-cli manifest
extend the existing host lifecycle acceptance test with repeated-install idempotence and interrupted-reinstall rollback assertions
forbidden_changes: naming a provider, registry, or fabric type on the hook or kernel path
letting an ingest failure, timeout, or unreachable daemon change the host's own hook answer
unbounded or unbudgeted ingest work on a host lifecycle event
minting a second admission or scope-identity path instead of reusing the host-neutral one the session-sync worker uses
turning the product test target or its feature on by default

dependency_direction_rules.reason: The capability contract cannot depend on fabric, any upper memory layer, root composition, or TraceDecay persistence, code-index, query, or semantic internals.
Fabric orchestrates capability contracts and cannot import or name a concrete provider implementation or SDK.
Final context assembly depends only on provider API/capability registry and TraceDecay application ports.
The Native adapter stays below fabric and cannot know external providers or the root binary crate.

Concrete adapters depend on the provider API and narrow application ports, never fabric, root composition, storage, database, code-index, query, or semantic internals; the provider registry is an explicit composition-layer exception.
NCM uses provider contracts and its licensed Biomem SDK/transport, never Native persistence, raw storage/private-filesystem engines, TraceDecay runtime internals, or a separate NCM/OCEAN adapter SDK.
Public transports expose provider-neutral application contracts.
Only the narrow composition/registry layer may construct concrete adapters.

exception_zones.reason: These crates own canonical Native persistence, lineage, schemas, transactions, graph publication, and recovery. Cognitive providers must sit above them.
required_exception_evidence: ADR proving no application/composition seam can satisfy the requirement
convergence-map entry with semantic invariants and rollback plan
Native parity and migration/recovery tests
policy revision if the zero-file zone cap is raised

exception_zones.reason: TraceDecay remains authority for current code and verified code projections; provider integration must consume ports rather than alter indexing semantics.
required_exception_evidence: ADR with rejected port-level alternatives
generation/staleness invariant tests
convergence-map entry and rebase plan
policy revision if the zero-file zone cap is raised

exception_zones.reason: Generated outputs must come from their owning catalog/generator or pinned dependency resolver, never manual provider edits.
required_exception_evidence: generator/catalog source touch in the same change
reproduction command and zero-drift receipt
convergence-map entry identifying generated output
ADR only when the generator contract itself changes

exception_zones.reason: Provider observation belongs after host-neutral admission. Host-specific edits multiply patch cost and risk different authority semantics per agent.
required_exception_evidence: ADR proving normalized host-neutral observation is insufficient
parity tests for every supported coding-agent host
convergence-map entry with removal plan
policy revision if the zero-file zone cap is raised

exception_zones.reason: Provider work must not weaken or silently reshape Zack's supported build, lint, test, or release lanes.
required_exception_evidence: ADR with upstream compatibility impact
clean baseline and cross-platform evidence
convergence-map entry and revert plan
policy revision if the zero-file zone cap is raised

notes: Revision patch-footprint.v2 is approved by product/architecture/adr/ADR-0011-patch-footprint-revision-v2.md: every cap equals the M4 observation-journey mount, M5 cognitive-recall port, Native configuration registration, and session-sync exact-scope footprint measured at that revision's tree plus at most roughly fifteen percent headroom. Per-entry line_budget values in the convergence map remain the binding limit for an individual file.

Revision patch-footprint.v3 is approved by product/architecture/adr/ADR-0014-host-hook-ingest-footprint-revision-v3.md: it carries every v2 cap forward unchanged except the three the Claude Code host hook ingest journey moves - upstream existing production files 34 -> 37, total upstream changed lines 3300 -> 3500, and exception-zone files 2 -> 4 - each set from the footprint measured at this revision's tree (37 production files, 3393 total changed lines, 4 exception-zone files) plus at most roughly fifteen percent headroom.
Added files under product_owned_paths are excluded from the upstream footprint totals.
Renaming or copying an upstream file counts as touching the destination and source.
Changed lines are additions plus deletions from git numstat against the immutable upstream floor.
Cargo.lock is a generated dependency-resolution output: it may change only with a workspace-manifest touch and a focused cargo metadata/build receipt; it is not a manually editable contract.

principles: Add product-owned crates and tests instead of embedding provider logic in Zack-owned crates.
Mount product behavior only at narrow application, daemon-composition, observation, recall, feedback, and configuration seams.
Every intentional edit to an upstream-owned existing file has one convergence-map entry with rationale, semantic invariants, focused verification, line budget, and rebase/removal plan.
Provider names are confined to product registry and adapters; upstream public transports and stores depend on capability contracts only.
Database internals, code-index internals, generated contracts, host-specific adapters, and toolchain/build policy are zero-touch zones unless an ADR proves the seam cannot be mounted elsewhere.
An exception does not silently raise the global budget: it requires both an ADR and an explicit policy revision when a hard cap would be exceeded.
scope: Pluggable-memory implementation through Native parity, NCM observer admission, the mounted observation journey (M4), cognitive recall integration (M5), and evaluation baselines (M8). Revision patch-footprint.v2 (ADR-0011) replaced the v1 caps with the footprint measured at its revision tree plus bounded headroom, and revision patch-footprint.v3 (ADR-0014) does the same for the Claude Code host hook ingest journey, which also adds the host_hook_ingest touch point and a two-file host-adapter exception. Later phases must either remain inside these caps or approve a new policy revision by ADR.
